{{nihongo|'''Narumi Hachimangū'''|鳴海八幡宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

=== Overview ===
It has been called "Hachiman" since ancient times, and was considered to be a separate shrine to {{ill|Narumi Shrine|Q11495515|qid=Q11495515}}. The location of the shrine was {{ill|Edago|Q11533553|qid=Q11533553}} in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Narumi Village}}, in the area that was called Zennoan Village in the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. The year of its founding is unknown, but there are records of shrine occupations dating back to the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, and a {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}} that is over 1,000 years old remains within the precincts, suggesting that it may be an old shrine that dates back to before the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}. As mentioned later, it is Shikinaisha's Ronsha.

Around this shrine, the remains of a village from the {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}}, ``Maenowa Ruins,'' have been discovered, and {{ill|Yayoi pottery|Q11487461|qid=Q11487461}} have been unearthed.

=== History ===
The company seems to have already existed in the Kamakura period, and there is a record that Motohisa Oga, the first generation member of the Kuno family, became a company official in the first year of {{ill|Jōei|Q1194168|qid=Q1194168}} ({{ill|1232|Q5418|qid=Q5418}}). Since ancient times, it has been called ``Hachimangu Shrine'' and was treated as a companion to Narumi Togu Shrine (Narumi Shrine). {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=During the Warring States period}}, there is a record that {{ill|Imagawa Yoshimoto|Q1054305|qid=Q1054305}} and {{ill|Yamaguchi Shigemasa|Q11467507|qid=Q11467507|lt=Chōjiro Shigemasa}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=corporate territory}} was {{ill|contribution|Q11455717|qid=Q11455717}} to our company and Narumi Togu Shrine.

According to ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Owari Makiyōki}},'' the priest Mr. Kuno submitted a document stating that Narumi Hachimangu Shrine is ``Kawahara Shrine,'' Aichi District, Owari Province, in ``{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}.'' According to ``{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}}'', there are some Edo-era fishing lanterns and {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}} that have the words ``Kawahara Shrine'' written on them.On the other hand, there is a theory that it corresponds to "Izoe Shrine" in Aichi District, Owari Province, but according to Kunihiko Sakakibara, a {{Sfn|Sakakibara|2004|pp=4}}{{Sfn|Sakakibara|2020|pp=64}}{{Efn|{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=local historian}}, Izoe Shrine was built during the Heian period. When it was abolished in the late period, Atsuta Daiguji disowned Hachimangu Shrine, and during the Oei era ({{ill|1394|Q6398|qid=Q6398}} to {{ill|1428|Q6315|qid=Q6315}}), the enshrinement site of Izoe Shrine, which had been abolished, was renamed to the old Jizoyama ({{jalink|Narumi Town) (Nagoya City)|Q136913130|Q136913130|Q136913130|Komatsuyama, Narumi Town), it is said to have been rebuilt as a Hachimangu Shrine in the former Tange (Kiyomizu Temple, Narumi Town). It is said that in the early Muromachi period, it was moved from that place to the present-day Azazenowa area, which was at the mouth of the {{ill|Ōgi River|Q11496839|qid=Q11496839|lt=Kurosuegawa}} large camphor tree. n|Sakakibara|2000|pp=88}}{{Sfn|Sakakibara|2004|pp=5}}{{Sfn|Sakakibara|2020|pp=64}}{{Sfn|Sakakibara|1984|pp=103}}. Izoe Shrine was later enshrined as Kitanosha, a subsidiary shrine of Hachimangu Shrine, but it is said to have been abolished in the Edo period {{Sfn|Sakakibara|2004|pp=5}}. }}, from the description in ``{{ill|Owari no Kuni Fudoki|Q135598023|qid=Q135598023}}'', it is presumed that Izoe Shrine was located in Aichi District {{ill|Aichi District|ceb|Aichi-gun|de|Aichi-gun|es|Distrito de Aichi (Aichi)|fa|شهرستان آیچی، آیچی|fr|District d'Aichi|hu|Aicsi körzet|id|Distrik Aichi, Aichi|it|Distretto di Aichi|ja|愛知郡 (愛知県)|ko|아이치군|pl|Powiat Aichi|ru|Айти (уезд)|tl|Distrito ng Aichi, Aichi|uk|Повіт Айті|vi|Aichi (huyện)|zh|愛知郡 (愛知縣)|qid=Q552687|lt=Hibego}}, and it is unreasonable to compare our company with Izoe Shrine.In {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}}3 ({{ill|1690|Q7678|qid=Q7678}}), he served as a priest at Narumi Shrine along with the Makino family.{{ill|Narumi-juku|Q3033344|qid=Q3033344}}The Kuno family of Honmachi moved to Maenowa and served as a priest.{{Sfn|Awakawa|2013|pp=47}}{{Sfn|Awakawa|2013|pp=48}}. In {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}}13 ({{ill|1700|Q6813|qid=Q6813}}), the Makino family priests and the Kuno family priests quarreled and the festival was divided. The parishioners from Sakumachi to Nakajima changed from those of Narumi Shrine to those of Hachimangu Shrine, and the festival began to be held in front and behind the scenes {{Sfn|Awakawa|2013|pp=48}}. In recent years, efforts have been seen to bring together the front and back sides of the festival and gather floats at Narumi-juku Honmachi.{{Sfn|Awakawa|2013|pp=35}}

=== Chronology ===

=== Precincts ===

=== Sacred tree ===
It is a large camphor tree with a trunk 8 meters in diameter.{{Sfn|Awakawa|2013|pp=47}}. It is said that it was already a large tree during the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, and is estimated to be 1000 to 1200 years old. In 2000 ({{ill|2000|Q1985|qid=Q1985}}), the Aichi Prefectural Arborist Association conducted treatment{{Sfn|Sakakibara|2004|pp=23}}.

=== Office ===
It was built in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}36 ({{ill|1903|Q2045|qid=Q2045}}) as the {{ill|Narumi|Q11675375|qid=Q11675375}} government building. {{Sfn|Sakakibara|2004|pp=14}} It was moved to its current location as a shrine office in July of 1931 ({{ill|1956|Q5221|qid=Q5221}}). It has been certified as a certified regional building asset by Nagoya City {{Sfn|Sakakibara|2000|pp=89}}.

=== Festival ===
In the past, the festival was held throughout the town on the same day as {{ill|Narumi Shrine|Q11495515|qid=Q11495515}}, which is also located in Narumi, but in {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}}13 ({{jalink |1700|Q6813}}), a dispute arose between the two shrines, and since then the festival has been divided into front (Narumi Hachiman Shrine) and back (Narumi Shrine) {{Sfn|Awakawa|2013|pp=34}}. In recent years, there have been efforts to unite the front and back sides and gather floats in Narumi-juku Honmachi, and the festival is now being held as before the festival was divided.{{Sfn|Awakawa|2013|pp=35}}

The Narumi Hachiman Shrine annual festival (Omote Festival) used to be held on August 15th, but since the first year of the Taisho era ({{ill|1912|ab|1912|af|1912|als|1912|am|1912 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1912|ar|1912|ary|1912|arz|1912|ast|1912|av|1912|avk|1912|az|1912|azb|۱۹۱۲ (میلادی)|ba|1912 йыл|ban|1912|bar|1912|bat_smg|1912|bcl|1912|be|1912|be_x_old|1912|bg|1912|bh|1912|bn|১৯১২|bpy|মারি ১৯১২|br|1912|bs|1912.|ca|1912|cdo|1912 nièng|ce|1912 шо|ceb|1912|ckb|١٩١٢|co|1912|crh|1912|cs|1912|csb|1912|cv|1912|cy|1912|da|1912|de|1912|diq|1912|dsb|1912|el|1912|eml|1912|eo|1912|es|1912|et|1912|eu|1912|ext|1912|fa|۱۹۱۲|fi|1912|fiu_vro|1912|fo|1912|fr|1912|frp|1912|frr|1912|fur|1912|fy|1912|ga|1912|gag|1912|gan|1912年|gcr|1912|gd|1912|gl|1912|gn|1912|gv|1912|hak|1912-ngièn|he|1912|hi|१९१२|hif|1912|hr|1912.|hsb|1912|ht|1912 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1912|hy|1912|hyw|1912 թուական|ia|1912|id|1912|ilo|1912|inh|1912 шу|io|1912|is|1912|it|1912|ja|1912年|jv|1912|ka|1912|kaa|1912|kab|1912|kbp|1912|kk|1912 жыл|kn|೧೯೧೨|ko|1912년|krc|1912 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1912|ku|1912|kv|1912-ӧд во|kw|1912|la|1912|lb|1912|lez|1912 йис|li|1912|lij|1912|lmo|1912|lt|1912 m.|lv|1912. gads|mai|१९१२|map_bms|1912|mdf|1912|mg|1912|mhr|1912|mi|1912|min|1912|mk|1912|ml|1912|mn|1912 он|mr|इ.स. १९१२|mrj|1912 и|ms|1912|my|၁၉၁၂|myv|1912 ие|mzn|۱۹۱۲|nah|1912|nap|1912|nds|1912|new|ई सं १९१२|nl|1912|nn|1912|no|1912|nov|1912|nrm|1912|nso|1912|oc|1912|olo|1912|or|୧୯୧୨|os|1912-æм аз|pa|1912|pam|1912|pap|1912|pl|1912|pnb|1912|pt|1912|qu|1912|ro|1912|roa_tara|1912|ru|1912 год|rue|1912|sah|1912|sc|1912|scn|1912|sco|1912|sd|1912ع|se|1912|sh|1912.|shn|1912|si|1912|simple|1912|sk|1912|sl|1912|smn|1912|sq|1912|sr|1912|srn|1912|stq|1912|su|1912|sv|1912|sw|1912|szl|1912|ta|1912|te|1912|tg|Соли 1912|th|พ.ศ. 2455|tk|1912|tl|1912|tly|1912|tpi|1912|tr|1912|tt|1912 ел|ty|1912|udm|1912 ар|ug|1912 - يىلى|uk|1912|ur|1912ء|uz|1912|vec|1912|vi|1912|vls|1912|vo|1912|wa|1912|war|1912|wuu|1912年|xmf|1912|yi|1912|za|1912 nienz|zea|1912|zh|1912年|zh_classical|一九一二年|zh_min_nan|1912 nî|zh_yue|1912年|qid=Q2077}}) it has been held on {{ill|September 15|Q2846|qid=Q2846}}, and since the Showa era it has been held on {{ill|October 15|Q2919|qid=Q2919}}. In recent years, the annual festival day has been set on a Saturday in the first half of {{ill|October|Q124|qid=Q124}}{{Sfn|Sakakibara|2005|pp=26}}.

At the Shōjo Festival, a giant doll called {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shōjō}} made of a bamboo framework with a red face mask and upper half of the body covered with a costume appears, and there is the ``Narumi Hachiman Shrine Reitaisai Festival'' (Omote Festival), where adults wear shōjō dolls and chase children around. Shōto is the deity of Narumi Hachimangu Shrine. The monkeys hit children with fake hands and sticks, and it is said that children who are hit by the monkeys do not get sick.{{Sfn|Awakawa|2013|pp=35}}.
